newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lacklustre talk.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Steady amid lacklustre talk.

text.p: Light distillate prices held steady in lacklustre trade with undertones a shade softer, traders said on Monday.
An European major was seen offering 50,000 barrels of 92-Ron supplies for loading July 8-12 at $23.35 but lowered its offer to $22.95 per barrel later Monday.
Limited bids were seen.
Traders said market fundamentals were a shade weaker due to fresh supplies from Thailand and the lack of buying interest.
A Japanese company is still a keen buyer, traders said.
Little was heard of Indonesian gasoline demand but the archipelago is expected to buy around 500,000 barrels per month in July and August on the back of refinery turnarounds.
Talk in the naphtha market was also thin with most traders' attention focused on an open-specification meeting currently going on in Japan.
Discussion at the meeting today was centred on expanding the origin of cargoes traded under the contract to include Indonesian heavy condensate.
The two-day meeting was expected to end on Tuesday.
A trader said Indonesia was expected to half its imports of naphtha, down to two cargoes instead of the usual four as two of its refineries are down on maintenance.
State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded two cargoes of
HAN, one for loading from Bombay between July 2-4 at a discount
of nearly $30 to Japanese naphtha spot quotes and the other from
Cochin between June 30-July 2 at a discount of $30-$35/T.
